Semi-annual commentary observed (e.g. H2-2024: 206m card payments, EUR 7bn, avg EUR 34).

candidates.why_relevant: Defines WHAT payment service providers must report to the central bank (instrument breakdowns, instant vs non-instant, remote vs terminal, e-money, mobile initiation). negative_findings.description: No official, recurring public statistical release of Flik transaction volumes, values or user counts was found from either Bankart or Banka Slovenije. Every quantitative Flik figure located (approximately 776k-800k+ users, ~1.5-2 million transactions per month, ~EUR 126m in a peak month, ~90% still P2P) originates from operator statements relayed through Slovenian media or association articles, not from a downloadable dataset.
negative_findings.result_summary: Flik metrics exist only as press-relayed operator claims; no primary series.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core indicator has no auditable primary source. Any Flik time series must be reconstructed from dated press citations with explicit provenance, and cannot be treated as official statistics. It also means displacement analysis versus cards/cash rests on the ECB/BSI credit-transfer aggregates rather than on scheme-level data.

negative_findings.description: No standalone Flik scheme website (e.g. a flik.si-style domain) was surfaced by either Slovenian- or English-language searching; all authoritative Flik material found sits under bankart.si (Flik Pay product and FAQ pages, merchant onboarding PDFs) or on individual bank pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Flik appears to have no independent public scheme site; Bankart is the hub.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design should centre on bankart.si plus per-bank pages rather than waiting for a scheme portal. Absence of a scheme site also explains the absence of a scheme statistics page.

negative_findings.description: Only Bankart's 2019 annual report PDF surfaced in searching (under bankart.si/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/). A 2023, 2024 or 2025 Bankart annual report with BIPS/TIPS/Flik volume figures was not located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bankart annual reports appear published but recent editions were not surfaced by search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bankart annual reports are the most likely place for audited BIPS transaction counts. Recent editions probably exist and are likely reachable via AJPES company filings (JOLP) or Bankart's own site navigation rather than via search engines; this should be pursued directly rather than recorded as unavailable.

negative_findings.description: No published transaction counts for the Slovenian interbank e-invoice exchange (operated via Bankart) or for UJP's eRačun flows were found. UJP publishes a register of e-invoice recipients and a list of contracted providers, but not volumes; the only quantified view located is a survey report from EPOS.
negative_findings.result_summary: E-invoicing rail is well documented structurally but not quantified publicly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: E-invoicing volume is a leading indicator for B2B A2A payment automation. Without it, the e-invoicing dimension of the cell rests on registry counts (recipients, providers) and survey estimates, which should be flagged as proxies.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenian aggregate statistic on PSD2 API call volumes, TPP counts or open-banking usage was located. Individual banks publish statutory API availability/performance disclosures and the Bankart HUB lists connected ASPSPs, but there is no national roll-up.
negative_findings.result_summary: Open-banking usage in SI is only measurable bank-by-bank or via the EBA/BSI licence registers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Claims about open-banking adoption in Slovenia will have to be built bottom-up from per-bank disclosures plus TPP licence registers, which is labour-intensive and should be scoped explicitly.

negative_findings.description: A Sberbank Slovenia PSD2 page (sberbank.si) still appears in search results although Sberbank Slovenia was absorbed into NLB in 2022. Similarly, Valú references found date to 2021/2022 and the current Valú product URL was not confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search results include defunct-institution and stale wallet pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The ASPSP/wallet register must be validated against current licensing rather than search results, or the source list will carry dead actors. Note these are unverified-status observations, not confirmed dead links.

coverage_gaps.description: The Banka Slovenije register of licensed payment institutions, e-money institutions and account information service providers, and the EBA central credit-institution/payment-institution register, were referenced in secondary sources but not directly located and pinned to a URL in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Directly navigate bsi.si to the supervision/register section ('register plačilnih institucij', 'družbe za izdajo elektronskega denarja', 'ponudniki storitev zagotavljanja informacij o računih') and pin the register URLs and any downloadable exports; do the same for the EBA credit institutions register filtered on SI.

coverage_gaps.description: Domestic acquiring/POS and A2A-adjacent actors were not searched in this pass: Halcom (corporate e-banking and payment software), Petrol Pay / Petrol's QR ecosystem, Nexi/Worldline activity in SI, Rekono (identity provider used for wallet onboarding), and small-bank Flik participants such as Delavska hranilnica and Gorenjska banka.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second sweep with queries such as 'Halcom takojšnja plačila', 'Petrol Pay QR plačilo statistika', 'Rekono identiteta plačila', 'Delavska hranilnica Flik' to complete the actor map for the A2A/wallet rail.

coverage_gaps.description: The ECB SPACE study (Study on the Payment Attitudes of Consumers in the Euro area) and any Banka Slovenije consumer payment-habits survey were not searched, yet these are the canonical bridge between instant/wallet adoption and cash usage at point of sale.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search for 'ECB SPACE study Slovenia' and 'Banka Slovenije raziskava plačilnih navad potrošnikov' and add the national SPACE country annex as a candidate; it is the main source linking this cell to the cash-usage topic.

coverage_gaps.description: SURS (Statistični urad RS) and its SiStat database were not queried for ICT/e-commerce usage indicators (share of individuals using mobile payments, internet banking penetration), which provide independent adoption denominators.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query SURS/SiStat for 'uporaba interneta bančništvo mobilna plačila' indicators and add the SiStat API/dataset as a candidate.

coverage_gaps.description: Public procurement portals (e-JN / Portal javnih naročil) and Diavgeia-equivalent transparency channels were not searched. Tenders for instant-payment, wallet or e-invoicing infrastructure reveal spend, vendors and roadmap ahead of any press release.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a sweep of the Slovenian public procurement portal for keywords 'plačilni sistem', 'takojšnja plačila', 'e-račun', 'mobilna denarnica' and register it as a recurring indirect source.

coverage_gaps.description: Several candidate URLs were assembled from actor knowledge rather than confirmed in a search result: the EPC SCT Inst register export path, the Wero/EPI domains, the ZBS Bančni vestnik e-archive root, the Valú product page and the AJPES eRacuni deep link.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route these through the deterministic liveness pass and replace any that redirect; treat them as unverified until then. None were fetched in this pass, so no liveness claim is made for any URL in this slice.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial market reports (GlobalData 'Slovenia Cards and Payments to 2028', Statista card-purchase series) surfaced but were not assessed for licensing or value.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide policy on paid syndicated research; if in scope, record GlobalData and Statista as licensed sources with cost and redistribution constraints rather than collecting them.

brief: Slovenia's instant/A2A landscape is structurally very well documented but poorly quantified in public: Banka Slovenije (payment instrument statistics, National Payments Council minutes, annual report) and the ECB Data Portal supply the authoritative aggregate series, while Bankart — operator of BIPS, the TIPS link, Flik, the Flik Pay gateway, the interbank e-invoice exchange and the national PSD2 HUB — is the single richest operator-side node and the natural centre of any collection design. The critical asymmetry for this cell is that Flik itself publishes no recurring statistics: every user, volume and value figure in circulation (roughly 776k–800k users, ~1.5–2m transactions monthly, a ~EUR 126m peak month, ~90% still P2P) reaches the public only through operator statements relayed by ZBS articles and Slovenian media, so a provenance-tagged press-citation series is unavoidable and must never be presented as official data. Wallet-side coverage is best tracked through structured vendor censuses (Apple's participating-banks list, Google Wallet's equivalent) diffed over time, plus per-bank product pages and the non-bank wallets mBills and Valú; the open-banking and e-invoicing legs are enumerable (Bankart HUB ASPSP list, per-bank statutory API disclosures, UJP's daily recipient register) but carry no published volume data. Priority follow-ups are the BSI/EBA licence registers, the ECB SPACE consumer study for the cash-substitution link, and recent Bankart annual reports via AJPES filings.
